title: bug: doctor run from WSL reports a live Windows daemon's daemon.json as stale, because it checks the Windows pid with kill -0, which WSL cannot see. TROUBLESHOOTING.md's "daemon.json is stale" fix then says rm .moe/daemon.json, so a WSL agent-mode seat that follows doctor deletes the live daemon's discovery file
description:
Hunt #17 (task-3488566e) found this as held item (a). It was re-run read-only from WSL at bb0bc17e on 2026-11-04; the evidence is in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-3488566e/mine/doctor-wsl-foreign-live.txt.
- `node <snapshot>/packages/moe-daemon/dist/index.js doctor --project /mnt/d/projexts/moes` prints `[WARN] daemon.json: daemon.json present but pid 36176 not running (stale)` and exits 0.
- daemon.json holds pid 36176, port 9876, bindHost wsl and projectPath D:/projexts/moes, so it is a Windows-owned record.
- In WSL, `kill -0 36176` gives "No such process".
- `curl http://172.26.208.1:9876/health` (the WSL gateway) answers healthy, with pid 36176 and projectPath D:/projexts/moes.

Cause: packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts:99-107 decides liveness with isProcessAlive(parsed.pid) alone. index.ts already handles a foreign record: isForeignDaemonInfo (:97), wslGatewayHost (:122), and validateDaemonInfoForProject (:357-380), which probes /health over loopback and then the WSL gateway. The launchers' sh pre-flight does the same, and it refuses to delete daemon.json when the probe fails. doctor reuses none of this.

Harm: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:75-82 ("daemon.json is stale", then `rm .moe/daemon.json`) has no liveness check. This repo runs in WSL agent mode, so following doctor's advice there deletes the live daemon's daemon.json. New proxies then cannot find the port, and a later start may launch a second daemon on the same .moe/.

Fix direction:
- For a foreign record (isForeignDaemonInfo), doctor's daemon.json probe asks /health over loopback, then over the WSL gateway.
- A reply whose projectPath is this project counts as alive: report pass and name the host that answered.
- Report stale only when no /health answers.
- In TROUBLESHOOTING's stale section, tell the reader to confirm /health does not answer before removing daemon.json, checking the WSL gateway too when in WSL, and never to remove it while /health answers.

Sequencing: this row depends on task-78fa7110 (relative --project), whose fix is expected to touch index.ts's foreign-daemon helpers. Plan against its landed shape and re-anchor the line numbers above.

Placement: task-3950184e also edits doctor.test.ts and TROUBLESHOOTING.md (around rows 1254-1255). Put this row's tests in their own describe block and edit only the stale section. No dependency edge is needed in worktree mode.
definitionOfDone: From WSL, take a daemon.json whose projectPath is a drive-letter path while a /health reporting the same project answers on loopback or the WSL gateway. Doctor's daemon.json probe must not report 'not running (stale)': it reports the daemon live and names the host that answered. A regression test in doctor.test.ts covers this foreign-live case with a stubbed health server, and a foreign-dead case (no /health answers) still warns stale.

The 'daemon.json is stale' section of docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md tells the reader to confirm /health does not answer before removing daemon.json, checking the WSL gateway as well when in WSL, as the launchers do. It also says never to remove daemon.json while /health answers.
The daemon tests for the touched files pass (doctor.test.ts, plus a test of any helper this row moves or shares), tsc is clean, and npm run lint passes at the repo root.

The stub /health servers report projectPath testDir, because doctor compares only /health's projectPath with --project and a temp dir is never a drive path off Windows. beforeEach spies fs.readFileSync so '/proc/net/route' returns a header-only table (no WSL gateway) unless a row appends `eth0 00000000 0200007F ...` (little-endian 127.0.0.2); every other path passes through to the captured real function. afterEach restores mocks, destroys sockets, closes servers and removes testDir. Rows: F1 loopback answers this project -> '[OK] daemon.json:' naming 127.0.0.1:, never 'not running' or 'stale', reachability [OK] naming the same, exit 0. F2 (skipIf not linux) 127.0.0.1:

answers another project and the gateway 127.0.0.2:

, exit 0. F3 x2 (DEAD_PID, and process.pid, a pid alive here) on an unused port -> '[WARN] daemon.json:' naming 127.0.0.1: and '(stale)', no reachability line, exit 0. F4 only another project answers -> daemon.json [WARN], reachability '[FAIL] ... reports a different project', exit 1. F5 a 503 'unhealthy' answer for this project -> daemon.json [WARN] without 'stale', reachability [WARN] naming HTTP 503, exit 0. The block imports only runDoctor, so run it against the unfixed tree first, in a snapshot (mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate): expect 6 failed. The architect's RED run of F1-F4 at 9f6857ee is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-d7b24cab/red-at-9f6857ee.log (5 failed, each for the bug's reason). Put your RED line in the completion summary.

Share the foreign-record helpers, with no behavior change. Move isForeignDaemonInfo (index.ts:87-100) and wslGatewayHost (index.ts:116-131) VERBATIM, doc comments included, into packages/moe-daemon/src/server/probeHost.ts as exports. Add `export async function foreignProbeHosts(info: Pick<DaemonInfo, 'bindHost'>, timeoutMs: number): Promise<string[]>`, which is today's inline host list from validateDaemonInfoForProject (index.ts:369-374): healthProbeAddress(recordedProbeHost(info), timeoutMs) when isLocalAddress holds it, then on Linux wslGatewayHost(), deduplicated. Read process.platform at call time, because index.test.ts's otherSide() flips it with Object.defineProperty. Use a DEFAULT `import fs from 'fs'` and extend the header note: doctor.test.ts stubs /proc/net/route through fs.readFileSync on that module object, and a named import would bypass the spy. In index.ts, import isForeignDaemonInfo and foreignProbeHosts on the existing probeHost import line, delete both moved functions, replace the foreign branch's host-list lines with `for (const host of await foreignProbeHosts(info, SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS))`, and keep isForeignDaemonInfo in the export block (index.test.ts X2 imports it from index.ts). error handling: foreignProbeHosts never throws (healthProbeAddress returns null for a non-string, failed or slow lookup; wslGatewayHost returns null on any read error). The repository-derived bindHost is still dialed only when isLocalAddress holds (mem:decision-daemon-cli-bindhost-local-rule, mem:gotcha-daemon-lifecycle-wsl-foreign). Do not edit index.test.ts: X2-X8 and B5 must pass unchanged.

doctor judges a foreign record by /health alone (packages/moe-daemon/src/commands/doctor.ts; transcribe the prototype hunk with the Edit tool). Import foreignProbeHosts and isForeignDaemonInfo. probeDaemonJson gains expectedProjectPath (runDoctor passes projectPath). When `typeof parsed.projectPath === 'string' && isForeignDaemonInfo({ projectPath })` holds, it returns probeForeignDaemonJson(port, pid, bindHost, expectedProjectPath) BEFORE isProcessAlive. A non-string projectPath is never foreign, because RegExp.test would coerce ['D:/x']. Extract endpoint(host, port) (IPv6 bracketed) and judgeHealthBody(body, where, expectedProjectPath, pid) out of probeDaemonReachability with byte-identical messages, so every local row and doctor.bindHost.test.ts B1-B5 stay unchanged. probeForeignDaemonJson asks each foreignProbeHosts address in order with probeHealth: no HTTP answer (statusCode undefined: refused, timed out, not HTTP) -> next address; a 200 JSON body -> judgeHealthBody; any other HTTP answer (503 from a live but unhealthy daemon, index.ts:767; 403; unparseable) -> warn '<where> answered but /health did not confirm a healthy Moe daemon (<error or HTTP n>)'. The first pass wins: '[OK] daemon.json valid: written on the other side of the WSL boundary (pid N, port P); /health answered on <where>', with that pass as the reachability line. Otherwise the first answer's verdict becomes the reachability line, and daemon.json warns '... /health on <where> answered but did not confirm this daemon'. Only when no address answers: '[WARN] ... no /health answered on <every endpoint asked, or a no-address reason> (stale)' and no reachability line. DaemonJsonProbe gains `foreignReachability?: ProbeResult | null`, which probeDaemonReachability returns first, so a foreign record is never re-dialed at the recorded loopback. error handling: probeHealth resolves an outcome on every error, timeout and oversize body, and foreignProbeHosts never throws. doctor still never signals, deletes or writes anything.

Edit nothing else in TROUBLESHOOTING.md.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: `moe-daemon doctor` judges a daemon.json written on the other side of the WSL boundary (isForeignDaemonInfo) by /health alone. It asks the addresses the daemon lifecycle asks (foreignProbeHosts: the recorded bindHost when it is this machine, then the WSL gateway on Linux). An answer confirming this daemon is reported live, naming the endpoint that answered. Any other HTTP answer is reported as the local probe would judge it, never as stale. It warns stale only when no address answers. TROUBLESHOOTING's stale section tells the reader to confirm /health does not answer (loopback or bindHost, plus the WSL gateway in WSL) before removing daemon.json, and never to remove it while /health answers for this project.
acceptanceCriteria: F1: a foreign record whose /health answers on loopback gives '[OK] daemon.json:' naming 127.0.0.1:<port>, never 'not running' or 'stale', and exit 0, though its pid is not alive here.
F2 (Linux): the WSL gateway's answer for this project beats loopback's answer for another project; both lines name the gateway endpoint.
F3: with no answer, it warns '(stale)' naming the endpoints asked, adds no reachability line and exits 0, whether or not the pid number is alive here.
F4: an answer only for another project is never green and exits 1. F5: a 503 answer for this project is never called stale.
Local-record doctor output and index.ts lifecycle behavior are unchanged (doctor.test.ts reachability rows, doctor.bindHost.test.ts B1-B5, index.test.ts X2-X8 and B5 pass unedited).
invariants: doctor never signals, deletes or writes anything.
A repository-derived bindHost is dialed only when isLocalAddress holds.
A foreign record is never judged by process.kill.
process.platform is read at call time.
compatibility: No MCP tool contract or daemon.json format change.

commands/doctor.ts: probeDaemonJson(moePath, expectedProjectPath), probeForeignDaemonJson, judgeHealthBody, endpoint, DaemonJsonProbe.foreignReachability.
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md: the body of '#### daemon.json is stale' only.
reuse: isForeignDaemonInfo and wslGatewayHost are moved, not copied.
One foreign host list (foreignProbeHosts) serves index.ts and doctor.
probeHealth and the extracted judgeHealthBody are reused for local and foreign records.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Copy the foreign host list into doctor: rejected. The reopenReason asks for reuse, and two copies drift; task-576e3005 moved the dial rule into server/probeHost.ts for exactly this reason. (2) doctor imports from index.ts: rejected. index.ts already imports doctor.ts (a cycle), and it reads env constants at load. (3) isForeignDaemonInfo in util/projectPath.ts: workable, but it would be a 6th file. probeHost.ts's stated purpose is the dial rule shared by the lifecycle and doctor, and isForeignDaemonInfo decides when the foreign rule applies. (4) Count only a 200 answer as 'answered': rejected. A live but unhealthy daemon answers 503 (index.ts:767) and would be called stale, which invites deleting its file (row F5). (5) Re-dial the found host in probeDaemonReachability: an unneeded second dial; the verdict travels in foreignReachability instead. (6) Flip process.platform in the doctor rows, as index.test.ts otherSide() does: rejected. The gateway row needs linux, and doctor's worktree probes would also run under the flip.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: doctor never compares daemon.json's projectPath with --project, only /health's, so the drive-letter fixture can keep the bug's literal while the stubs name testDir. probeHealth never throws. /health answers 503 with the same JSON body when unhealthy. CI runs the daemon vitest suite on ubuntu only (ci.yml test:coverage); the 3-OS matrix only builds the daemon. Prototype: +210/-59 source and test lines across 4 files (doctor.test.ts +101/-1, doctor.ts +59/-19, probeHost.ts +47/-1, index.ts +3/-38), plus about 15 doc lines, well under the 400 net-LOC review cap. Six mutants were each killed: first answer wins, mismatch counted as live, no gateway, recorded host never asked, a pid gate on the foreign branch, and re-dialing the recorded host. An eighth mutant, only 200 counts as an answer, is killed by F5. Logs: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-d7b24cab/{red-at-9f6857ee.log,green.log}.
planningNotes.risks:
F2 binds 127.0.0.1 and 127.0.0.2 on the same port. Linux routes all of 127/8 to lo; other platforms skip the row. An EADDRINUSE on 127.0.0.1:

would be a rare flake. The fs.readFileSync spy must pass every other path through, using the real function captured before spying. The move must keep process.platform read at call time and the default fs import; otherwise index.test.ts X3/B5 or doctor F2 break. The worker should use the Edit tool for tracked files (global rail), using the prototype diff as reference, never git apply. A peer editing the same TROUBLESHOOTING lines would conflict at landing; no open row edits that section now. Error handling and test coverage are both in the steps.
